hook.text: A fighting-game 'DUO vs OSCAR' card, whip pans between the two plush rivals, and Oscar shattering Duo's king, followed by 'Another win for Oscar, but hey we all have to start somewhere.'
hook.technique_other: cold-open comedy sketch: a rival mascot beats the brand mascot at chess before any product is shown

cta.text: LEARN CHESS on duolingo (spoken: 'download Duolingo for free in the app store', w133-w139)

summary.tone: Playful, absurdist, self-aware comedy. A smug mascot narrates in character, with a fast mixed-media pace (plush puppetry, 3D, recreated app UI, flat illustration) and pop-culture parodies (talk show, music video, keynote 'one more thing').

signature_moments.description: A crown drops onto the throned Oscar against a starburst flash. A zoom-through lands on a gold-framed board where a knight forks him ('Fork, baby. Fork.') and topples the throne under an outlined 'ADVANCED TACTICS' label.
signature_moments.why_premium: A feature name is turned into a staged, sound-synced visual gag (whoosh and impact on the crown) instead of a screenshot, so the feature is remembered and the craft reads as expensive.

signature_moments.description: Oscar spins next to a boombox and raises the phone. A lightning bolt strikes it in a darkened frame, and he is left scorched with a smoking, burning moustache while the phone plays the app's animations.
signature_moments.why_premium: Practical-looking VFX (exposure dip, additive glow, fire and smoke sims) on a soft plush character give an ordinary feature like new animations a cinematic payoff.

signature_moments.description: On the end card, copies of Oscar rain down and pile up around the hero figure under 'LEARN CHESS on duolingo', ending on a long music-only tail.
signature_moments.why_premium: A physics-sim payoff in a single locked lockup keeps the brand name on screen for 30 s, and the motion stays lively with no extra copy.

hook.evidence: Within 7 s it sets up a versus card and a rival, whip pans between the plush players on reverse-swoosh SFX, and pays off with the king shattering on an impact (x007). The first VO line lands the premise. The product itself does not appear until s010/s011.

clarity.evidence: Each feature gets its own labelled beat: lessons on the course path, basic moves, ADVANCED TACTICS, THOUSANDS OF PUZZLES, playing a match, animations, ELO PROGRESS, STALEMATE HELPER!, and coming-soon play against other learners. The comic density and very fast cuts (many shots under 1 s) sometimes bury the UI, and the closing twist (s045-s048) is not obvious.

ui_showcase.evidence: The UI is recreated cleanly and on-brand (course switcher, lesson path, move-hint dots, ELO chart, stalemate helper board, opponent cards), but each screen is brief and the characters dominate it. Real app capture appears only small, on in-hand phones.

motion_polish.evidence: Very well-crafted mixed media: puppeted plush footage with shallow focus, 3D throne and lightning scenes, zoom-through and push transitions, a circular iris mask into the keynote parody, a WINNER/LOSER triptych with an RGB-split stamp-in, and a rigid-body plush rain on the end card. Motion blur is used consistently on every fast move.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchor audio facts plus visuals. 89 SFX candidates over 111 s, with reverse swooshes on almost every opening cut (x002-x006), impacts on the king shatter (x007), the crown (x015) and the boom/lightning beats, and a music bed at about 94 BPM. Integrated loudness is -15.83 LUFS. The end card is about 23 s of music only. Many candidates are labelled 'unsure', so the exact SFX mapping is uncertain.

vo_script_quality.evidence: In-character VO that is tight and joke-driven: 'Fork, baby. Fork.', 'Whoopsie! I won.', the 'one more thing' parody, and a mock side-effects disclaimer in the CTA. Every feature line is short and lands on its visual. The transcript is garbled in places (e.g. w72, w82, w139), so some lines could not be checked.

brand_consistency.evidence: Duolingo green dominates and the outlined heavy italic all-caps label style recurs throughout. Duo and Oscar come from the app's own cast, the recreated UI matches the app, and the end card uses the brand wordmark. The tone fits the brand's known mascot-comedy voice.

works_muted.evidence: Baked-in labels carry several features (ADVANCED TACTICS, THOUSANDS OF PUZZLES, STALEMATE HELPER!, ONE MORE THING..., WINNER/LOSER, LEARN CHESS on duolingo) and the visual gags read without sound. However, the lessons, basic moves, real match, animations and ELO beats, the coming-soon framing, and 'download for free' exist only in the VO.

overall.evidence: A premium-crafted, very entertaining launch that turns a feature list into a chain of mascot sketches with consistent branding and strong motion and VFX. It falls short of best-in-class as a product explainer because the UI appears only briefly, it relies on the VO, and the 30 s end card is long.

localization_friendliness.notes: Feature titles are baked into stylised outlined artwork (ADVANCED TACTICS, THOUSANDS OF PUZZLES, STALEMATE HELPER!, ONE MORE THING..., WINNER/LOSER, LEARN CHESS), and the recreated UI holds English strings. The humour depends on puns in a character voice ('Fork, baby', the side-effects disclaimer), which are hard to translate. Localizing it would mean re-rendering the type, re-casting the voice and rewriting jokes. The plush and 3D visuals themselves are language-neutral.

pattern.description: In a shallow-depth-of-field 3D chess scene, the white king fractures in place and collapses into a pile of faceted white shards while the surrounding black pieces stay still.
pattern.why_premium: A physically simulated fracture with real-feeling weight, faceted shards and tactile CG materials turns a narrative beat (the opponent's king is beaten) into a punchy visual punchline, sold by a synced impact hit.

build_hint.gsap: Pre-render the fracture as a 3D sim (image sequence/video); in HyperFrames play it with a hard cut-in, then add gsap.fromTo(shardsLayer, {y: 0}, {y: 6, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power2.in'}) and a 2-frame camera shake (x: +/-4, ease: 'steps(2)') on impact.
build_hint.remotion: Use <OffthreadVideo> or an image sequence of the rendered shatter; optional impact shake translateX = 4 * Math.sin(frame * 3) * Math.max(0, 1 - (frame - impactFrame) / 6) for 6 frames.

events.notes: Rendered 3D footage; the motion is a physics sim, so easing is not meaningful. f183 is motion blur from the incoming shot transition, not part of the shatter. b02 (tiny right-edge box) is noise and is not listed.

pattern.description: The out-of-focus Duo plush hops up behind the white pieces, tilting slightly mid-air, and drops back to its starting spot within roughly a third of a second, with heavy motion blur; the foreground pieces stay put.
pattern.why_premium: A quick, physical character hop puts brand personality into a product beat: the mascot reacts like a living opponent, and the shallow focus plus real motion blur make the tabletop scene feel tactile and handmade instead of flat CG.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.timeline().to(mascot, {y: -90, rotation: -4, duration: 0.17, ease: 'power2.out'}).to(mascot, {y: 0, rotation: 0, duration: 0.18, ease: 'power2.in'}).to(mascot, {scaleY: 0.96, scaleX: 1.03, duration: 0.06, yoyo: true, repeat: 1, ease: 'sine.inOut', transformOrigin: '50% 100%'}); add motion blur via a short filter: 'blur(3px)' at peak velocity.
build_hint.remotion: const hop = Math.sin(Math.PI * Math.min(1, frame / 11)); translateY = -90 * hop; rotate = -4 * hop; on landing apply a squash with spring({frame: frame - 11, fps, config: {damping: 12, stiffness: 300}}) mapped to scaleY 0.96->1.

events.notes: facts.json reports camera.move = tilt_down, but the foreground chess pieces look stationary across the filmstrip; the motion appears to be the mascot hopping (live-action/stop-motion plush), so the tilt verdict is probably driven by the large moving mascot. Worth a human check. Only one full-frame candidate box (b01) exists. No SFX candidates.

pattern.description: A close-up of the rook with grey move-hint dots snaps out to a wider view of the illustrated board corner. The move dots clear, then a gold star pops above the rook and bursts into a dashed ring of particles that fades around the piece as the frame settles.
pattern.why_premium: Fast, snappy reframes keep the tutorial lively without a camera move, and the star-to-particle-ring reward reuses Duolingo's own success feedback, so the tutorial already feels like the product.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to(boardGroup, {scale: 0.6, x: 120, y: 60, duration: 0.2, ease: 'power3.out'}); tl.to(moveDots, {autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.08}, '<'); tl.fromTo(star, {scale: 0, autoAlpha: 0}, {scale: 1, autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.12, ease: 'back.out(3)'}); tl.to(star, {scale: 0.2, autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.08, ease: 'power2.in'}); tl.fromTo(ringDots, {scale: 0.4, autoAlpha: 1}, {scale: 1.2, autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power2.out', stagger: {each: 0.01, from: 'random'}}, '<'); tl.fromTo(rook, {y: 0}, {y: -6, duration: 0.06, yoyo: true, repeat: 1, ease: 'sine.out'}, '<');
build_hint.remotion: Board scale/translate with interpolate(frame, [0, 6], [1, 0.6], {easing: Easing.out(Easing.cubic)}); star scale via spring({frame: frame - 13, fps, config: {damping: 8, stiffness: 400, mass: 0.6}}) then fade over 3 frames; ring dots radius = interpolate(frame - 15, [0, 9], [20, 70]) with opacity 1->0; rook hop translateY = -6 * Math.sin(Math.PI * clamp((frame - 14) / 4)).

events.notes: The energy curve has a near-zero dip mid-burst (frames 590/591), so the board reframes may be hard jump-cuts between framings rather than one continuous zoom; camera.move is 'none', so this is reported as a content re-layout, not a camera move. Grey move-hint dots disappear but have no position on the end frame, so they are not listed separately. Rook and star/ring use manual boxes (only b01 offered). No SFX candidates.

pattern.description: A fast snap pull-out (about 0.80x scale over about 4 frames) from a close-up of the character to a medium shot that reveals the interviewer's mic at the left edge, landing on 'some big' in the narration.
pattern.why_premium: Abrupt sitcom-style zoom cuts set comic rhythm without a hard cut, and the reveal of the off-screen mic adds context in the same move.

build_hint.gsap: Camera container starts scaled: gsap.fromTo(camera, {scale: 1.25}, {scale: 1, duration: 0.13, ease: 'expo.out', transformOrigin: '50% 40%'}); the mic layer sits outside the initial crop so it enters naturally as the scale drops.
build_hint.remotion: scale = interpolate(frame, [start, start + 4], [1.25, 1], {easing: Easing.out(Easing.exp), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) on an AbsoluteFill wrapper; no spring (no overshoot visible).

events.notes: Camera verdict pull_out (scale 0.80); the motion is almost all camera. Most diff boxes (b03, b05-b09) are curtain-fold slivers and are not listed. b04 is the closest box for the mic; it is a column strip, not a tight box. No SFX candidates.

elements.label: 3D character (Oscar) in the chair, shrinking in frame as the camera snaps out
Interviewer's microphone and hand entering at the left edge as the frame widens

pattern.description: A second snap pull-out (about 0.77x scale over about 4 frames) continuing from e008: medium shot to a wide stage two-shot that reveals the interviewer is a lookalike character, landing just before the repeated 'big' in 'big, big plans'.
pattern.why_premium: Two stepped snap zooms echo the narration's repetition ('big, big'), and the final widen pays off as a visual gag (the interviewer is his double) with no extra cut.

build_hint.gsap: Same camera container as e008, second step: tl.to(camera, {scale: 1, y: '+6%', duration: 0.13, ease: 'expo.out'}) after a hold of about 0.55 s from a scale of about 1.3; both steps use identical durations and eases so the rhythm reads as deliberate.
build_hint.remotion: Piecewise interpolate on the wrapper scale: [1.6, 1.6 -> 1.3 over 4 frames, hold, 1.3 -> 1 over 4 frames] with Easing.out(Easing.exp), clamp; no spring.

events.notes: Camera verdict pull_out (scale 0.766, pan_y -0.063); motion is almost all camera. b02 is an OCR misread ('6') on Oscar's face, used here as the nearest box to the main subject. b03 is a curtain-fold sliver. No SFX candidates.

pattern.description: Live-action puppet shot: a fast camera push-in (about 1.2x) punches in on the mascot as he raises an arm and speaks, background chess pieces blurring further with shallower depth of field.
pattern.why_premium: A short, snappy punch-in timed to the punchline ('too well') adds comedic emphasis and energy without a cut, keeping continuity on the character's performance.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.fromTo('.scene', {scale: 1, yPercent: 0}, {scale: 1.2, yPercent: -2.5, duration: 0.17, ease: 'power2.inOut'}); background layer: fromTo filter blur(4px)->blur(8px) same timing; arm gesture as a separate rotate tween (power2.out, 0.3s) starting slightly before the zoom.
build_hint.remotion: const s = interpolate(frame, [0, 5], [1, 1.2], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.quad), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); apply transform: scale(s) translateY(-2.5%) on the scene container; arm via interpolate rotate with Easing.out(Easing.quad) over ~9 frames.

events.notes: Live-action/puppet footage, not UI; camera verdict push_in (scale 1.198). Energy curve has a near-zero frame mid-burst (duplicate frame), possibly a speed-ramped zoom. b02 OCR text 'ho' is a misread of the arm. No SFX candidates.

pattern.description: A large close-up of the mascot in front of the 'LEARN CHESS' title drops rapidly downward with heavy motion blur, exiting the bottom of the frame and revealing a small full-body version of the same character standing on a base beneath the static title.
pattern.why_premium: Gravity-driven exit of the foreground subject reframes from close-up to hero lockup without a cut; the motion blur sells speed and the static title anchors the composition, giving a playful, tactile end-card resolve.

build_hint.gsap: Title stays static. gsap.to('.closeup', {yPercent: 120, duration: 0.13, ease: 'power3.in', filter: 'blur(6px)'}); small figure already in place behind (z-index below) or gsap.set visible at the same moment; optional tiny settle on the small figure with back.out.
build_hint.remotion: const y = interpolate(frame, [0, 4], [0, 120], {easing: Easing.in(Easing.cubic), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); closeup style transform: translateY(y%) plus filter blur proportional to velocity; render the small figure underneath, static.

events.notes: Live-action/puppet compositing on green background. Before the drop the close-up wobbles/turns (energy from frame 1). Camera verdict none. Spectrogram shows a downward sweep around 82.72s that may be a whoosh, but no SFX candidates were given, so none reviewed. The close-up element uses manual_box because it has left the frame by the end frame.

pattern.description: Duplicate mascot plushes keep dropping into frame from the top, bouncing and tumbling around the static hero figure on its pedestal while the 'LEARN CHESS' / 'on duolingo' lockup stays fixed.
pattern.why_premium: Physical, gravity-driven chaos around a calm, static hero and title creates comedic energy in the end card; real objects with motion blur and contact shadows feel tactile and on-brand rather than templated.

build_hint.gsap: Keep title, subtitle and hero static. For each drop: gsap.fromTo(item, {y: -800, rotation: gsap.utils.random(-40, 40)}, {y: 0, rotation: gsap.utils.random(-90, 90), duration: 0.45, ease: 'bounce.out'}) with a staggered, irregular start (stagger: {each: 0.3, from: 'random'}); add a small x drift and blur(4px)->0 during the fall.
build_hint.remotion: Per item: const s = spring({frame: frame - delay, fps, config: {mass: 1, stiffness: 180, damping: 9}}); translateY = interpolate(s, [0, 1], [-800, 0]); rotate = interpolate(s, [0, 1], [r0, r1]); irregular delays per item; hero and text layers untouched.

events.notes: Live-action/puppet compositing on green; camera verdict none (scale 1.097 reflects the large foreground plush, not a camera move). b01 is a union box spanning several items, not used. The left cluster b02 contains several plushes; treated as one group.

pattern.description: Continuation of the end-card gag: another duplicate plush falls from above with heavy motion blur, passes behind the 'on duolingo' overlay and lands face-down in the centre foreground, now partly covering the hero figure in an ever-growing pile.
pattern.why_premium: Escalating physical comedy on a fixed typographic lockup; the text stays on top and legible while real objects with motion blur and soft contact shadows add tactile, handmade energy.

build_hint.gsap: Text layers static and above the object layer. gsap.fromTo('.plush', {y: -900, rotation: -30, filter: 'blur(8px)'}, {y: 0, rotation: 10, filter: 'blur(2px)', duration: 0.4, ease: 'power3.in'}) followed by a short squash/settle (scaleY 0.92 -> 1, ease 'back.out(2)', 0.15s).
build_hint.remotion: const y = interpolate(frame - delay, [0, 12], [-900, 0], {easing: Easing.in(Easing.cubic), extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); then a spring({frame: frame - delay - 12, fps, config: {stiffness: 300, damping: 12}}) driving a small squash; keep text layers above and static.

events.notes: Live-action/puppet compositing. 'on duolingo' (b03) and 'LEARN CHESS' are static overlays; b03 only registers change because the plush passes behind it, so it is not listed. b02 is a union box over the fall path, not used to avoid duplicating the same plush. No SFX candidates; the spectrogram shows only rhythmic music.
